findings.population: Washington University undergraduates aged18–24, course credit
findings.context: Laboratory learning of two short TOEFL-style prose passages
findings.locator: Experiment1 methods/results, Figure1 pp250–251; author-hosted PDF
findings.design: Counterbalanced within-person practice comparison with between-person retention interval
findings.sample: N120 total across5min/2day/1week conditions; subgroup N not inferred
findings.exposure: After7min reading,7min title-cued free recall without feedback
findings.comparator: After7min reading,7min restudy of same passage
findings.measurement: Proportion of30idea units recalled in10min under same passage title; excludes mere word-order matching
findings.result: Initial retrieval yielded higher delayed idea-unit recall than matched-time restudy.
findings.limitations: Restricted cue/material/age/sample; counterbalancing documented, random allocation not claimed; no general knowledge profile, capacity or calibration effect.

findings.population: Washington University undergraduates aged18–24, course credit
findings.context: Laboratory learning of two short TOEFL-style prose passages
findings.locator: Experiment1 Figure1 and result comparisons pp250–251
findings.result: Restudy produced higher immediate recall than retrieval practice.
findings.limitations: OUTSIDE delayed signed scope; contradicts universal/immediate improvement, not the qualified2day/1week claim. No zero-effect inference.

findings.population: Washington University undergraduates aged18–24, course credit
findings.context: Laboratory learning of two short TOEFL-style prose passages
findings.exposure: One study plus three free-recall tests
findings.comparator: Four study periods or three study periods plus one test
findings.result: Repeated testing favored one-week recall, but restudy favored five-minute recall.
findings.limitations: Study periods5min and test periods10min: not matched total time, no simple dose-response or independent replication from multiple outcomes. Broader protocol is not exact Exp1 operation.

findings.population: Washington University undergraduates aged18–24, course credit
findings.context: Laboratory learning of two short TOEFL-style prose passages
findings.sample: SameN180; repeated outcomes not new trial
findings.measurement: Self-reported ease/difficulty of reading passage, not audience-fit RDS
findings.result: No group difference in perceived readability was detected.
findings.limitations: OUTSIDE accessibility endpoint; not equivalence, actual text readability or RDS change. Future-recall prediction in same table is not PSY-068 current memory-confidence measure.

findings.population: Participants in included retrieval/restudy studies; individual demographics not extracted
findings.design: Meta-analytic review of testing versus restudy
findings.exposure: Initial retrieval tasks, including recall and recognition
findings.result: Recall testing benefits retention more than recognition testing in the review; effort/episodic accounts remain alternatives.
findings.limitations: Potential primary/review overlap; exact benchmark study not independent replication. Limited support for semantic-elaboration theory is not causal mediation.

findings.population: Eyewitness-video participants; detailed demographics/N not extracted
findings.context: Eight-photo target-present/absent lineups with unbiased offender-absent instructions
findings.timing: After initial identification/rejection, with rating time/form varied
findings.comparator: Identification/nonidentification comparisons with differing feedback conditions
findings.measurement: Current and retrospective confidence, response latency, correct/mistaken IDs and lineup rejections
findings.result: Confirming feedback inflated certainty for correct/mistaken identifications and rejections; effect depended on rating format and latency.
findings.limitations: Exact current-confidence comparator, item and subgroup contrast not extracted; retrospective certainty is not independent current accuracy. Research ethics/legal constraints unassessed; no permission implied.

findings.design: Same two experiments; secondary calibration/association contrasts
findings.measurement: Confidence-accuracy correlation and overconfidence, not true memory strength
findings.result: Feedback did not alter the confidence-accuracy correlation while producing overconfidence.
findings.limitations: Nondetected correlation change does not mean calibration preserved; correlation and calibration differ. OUTSIDE exact subjective-confidence target; no accuracy benefit.

happeningTypes.name: Practice free recall of specified previously studied material without feedback
happeningTypes.description: Attempt retrieval of specified previously studied material under a declared cue, without corrective feedback during the practice interval. Identity does not promise retention, accurate knowledge, transfer, confidence, efficacy or practitioner permission. Study/test schedule and cue belong in effect scope.
happeningTypes.constraints: Actor control, prerequisites, feasibility, legality, ethics/risk and applicability NOT_ASSESSED. No automatic recommendation; avoid high-stakes testing or clinical transfer without independent assessment.

happeningTypes.name: Provide specified confirming feedback after a lineup response
happeningTypes.description: Deliver a specified message confirming a participant's identification or lineup-rejection response after it is made. The identity describes the research operation only: no accuracy, confidence benefit, efficacy, truthful validation or practitioner permission is implied.
happeningTypes.constraints: Risk of memory contamination, overconfidence and legal harm; not a recommendation or authorization to manipulate witnesses. Control, prerequisites, feasibility, lawful/ethical permission and context applicability NOT_ASSESSED.

assertions.scope: After7min initial reading of specified short prose, one7min title-cued free-recall attempt without feedback versus7min restudy can increase probability of retrieving that prose's idea units under the same title cue at2days or1week among comparable18–24year-old undergraduates. Five-minute tests explicitly excluded from signed increase.
assertions.measurement: Proportion of30scored idea units retrieved in a10min title-cued final free-recall test. Exact memory/material and current cue specified; not recall latency, recognition, whole DomainKnowledge profile, general memory capacity or future-learning prediction.
assertions.timing: Practice follows initial study; effect measured at2days/1week only. No onset between measured points, lifetime durability or all-cue transfer asserted.
assertions.risk: Counterbalanced controlled study not asserted randomized; narrow sample/materials/cue and scoring limits. Immediate5min reversal explicit. Exp2 unequal study/test durations not an identical dose contrast. No comprehension, calibration, confidence, readiness across all memories, trait change or practitioner permission.
assertions.mechanism: Retrieval practice may modify subsequent access routes; episodic-context and effort accounts remain alternatives, not independently identified mediators.
assertions.rationale: Primary Exp1 matched-time comparison supports later same-cue recall probability, a canonical accessibility indicator. Immediate reverse and broader heterogeneous protocols require a MIXED synthesis and strict temporal/material boundary; no independent replication count or generic memory benefit.
assertions.contributionReconciliation: One operation/material/cue contribution. No parallel knowledge, familiarity or mediated retention contribution inferred; primary and review evidence not summed.

assertions.scope: Specified confirming post-identification feedback in video/photolineup experiments; exact current-versus-retrospective confidence estimand and comparator unresolved.
assertions.measurement: Current confidence that specified identification/recollection is accurate must be separated from retrospective initial certainty, confidence-accuracy correlation and objective accuracy.
assertions.timing: Feedback after response; exact current rating interval and contamination sequence require extraction.
assertions.risk: Feedback may inflate overconfidence without accuracy; no benefit, lawful/ethical permission or recommendation. Adult pristine initial lineup evidence is not post-feedback validation.
assertions.mechanism: External confirmation may alter subjective interpretation of memory reliability; does not change original event or demonstrate memory correctness.
assertions.rationale: Controlled studies support certainty inflation broadly, but abstract-level current/retrospective contrasts are not sufficiently separated for exact signed Driver effect. Preserve calibration null and overconfidence, not a trust/accuracy benefit.
